Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of $\displaystyle \int_{-4}^4 f(x) \,\textrm{d}x.$
examples.worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the arc of a semi-circle for $x\in [-4,0],$ a line segment for $x\in (0,2),$ a line segment for $x\in (2,4],$ and the point at $x=2.$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+0+{{{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in [-4,0].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle with a radius of $2,$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (0,2).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x = -A_2 = -2.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x \in (2,4].$  The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =2\pi -2+2 \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the line segment for $x\in [-5,-2],$ the line segment for $x\in (-2,1],$ the line segment for $x\in (1,3],$ and the line segment for $x\in [3,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{4}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,-2].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3\cdot 3) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-2,1].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh \\  & =3\cdot 1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-3.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (1,3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot 2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,4].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}+{A}_{4} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}-3+2+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
